dedupe_keys.name: reservoir flood extents for large raised reservoirs england dry day and wet day

description: The Reservoir Flood Extents of the Environment Agency map the land in England that could flood if a large raised reservoir failed and released its water. For each reservoir two scenarios are modelled: a dry day, when local rivers are at normal levels, and a wet day, when rivers have already overflowed their banks, plus a layer showing the river flooding that contributes to the wet-day outline. The maps come from the Reservoir Flood Mapping Project and cover all large raised reservoirs in operation in October 2016. They are offered as national dry-day and wet-day layers and as per-reservoir packages, through WMS, WFS and OGC API Features and as file geodatabase, GeoJSON, GeoPackage and Shapefile downloads with a data guide, free under the Open Government Licence with no access constraints; the national layers were last modified in June 2026 and are listed as updated quarterly. Caveats: each outline is a credible worst case that says nothing about the likelihood of failure, smaller reservoirs and those commissioned after October 2016 are missing, and depths and velocities are not part of these outline layers. Simulation uses: dam-break exposure of people, buildings and infrastructure downstream, emergency and evacuation planning, cascading failure from reservoirs to roads, power and water assets, and prioritising reservoir safety work. Related records: EA flood defence assets (data-ea-aims-spatial-flood-defences) and the Spanish dam inventory (data-spain-dam-reservoir-inventory).
